request.user:
Subject: Botany
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

The absolute refractory period during an action potential generation is primarily caused by:
(A) Closure of voltage-gated K^+ channels.
(B) Inactivation of voltage-gated Na^+ channels.
(C) Increased permeability to Cl^− ions.
(D) Continuous activation of the Na^+/K^+ pump.

result.working: During the action potential, depolarisation opens voltage-gated Na+ channels. They then enter an inactivated state through the inactivation gate, and cannot reopen until the membrane repolarises and the gate resets. While they are inactivated, no stimulus of any strength can trigger another action potential. This is the absolute refractory period. K+ channels remaining open causes the relative refractory period and hyperpolarisation. Cl- permeability and the Na+/K+ pump are not the main cause.
result.note: The question is filed under Botany but it is a neurophysiology (Zoology) topic.
